The auto-dismiss clock is a real pause/resume, not a restart: `holdClock()` subtracts elapsed time into `remaining` and `runClock()` re-arms with the remainder. Undo reuses .btn--ghost and then nullifies border-color to transparent — visually correct (no box-in-box) but semantically muddy, since the variant's defining property is overridden at every state.
votes.worst_defect: The optical spacing inside the action cluster: a uniform 16px gap token laid over button padding and a 44px tap target produces ~16/32/46px steps, leaving a conspicuously wide gap between "Undo" and the dismiss ×, which is the one place the rendered component's rhythm visibly disagrees with its own spacing scale.

strengths: All three required affordances exist and are genuinely distinct outcomes: inline Undo (`close('undo')` then `revert(previous)` — restores the prior value, cancels the pending server ack, and replaces the toast with a shorter 4s revert notice), a 6s auto-dismiss (`close('timeout')`), and an explicit × dismiss with `aria-label="Dismiss"` plus a global Esc path (`close('dismiss')` / `close('escape')`) that closes without touching the value. The readout (`state saved · undo available` → `dismissed · <reason>`) makes the distinction observable.

The optimistic semantics are actually modelled, not just claimed: `commit(next)` mutates the setting before any acknowledgement, `setServer('pending')` flips to `acknowledged` at a simulated 900ms, and undo inside that window clears `ackTimer` and reports `rolled back`. The screenshot confirms the ground state — value already reads "Daily" while the snackbar is still up.

The auto-dismiss clock is genuinely held for both pointer and keyboard: `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` pause/resume, and `focusin`/`focusout` with a `root.contains(event.relatedTarget)` guard so moving between Undo and the × does not spuriously restart the countdown. Pause snapshots `deadline - Date.now()` into `remaining` and resume re-bases the deadline, so no time is lost or double-counted, and the readout shows `Ns · held`.

Lifecycle correctness is unusually careful for this component class: an inline accent hairline visualises remaining time driven from JS (`--snackbar-remaining`) so it is unaffected by the reduced-motion transition clamp; stale callbacks are fenced with a `live !== mine` generation guard so a replaced snackbar cannot reset harness state; and `close()` has a `setTimeout` fallback so a non-firing `transitionend` never orphans the node.
defects: The live region is created already populated and then inserted (`role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` set on the new node before `column.appendChild(root)`). Screen readers generally announce mutations *inside* an existing live region, not the insertion of a pre-filled one, so a time-limited Undo can be silent to AT users. The persistent `#snackbar-column` wrapper is right there and is not the live region.

Copy restates the saved object rather than only what happened: "Digest set to Daily." echoes the label and value rendered directly above it, and the revert toast doubles down with "Change reverted." + "Digest is back to Weekly." Neither sells nor apologises, but both re-narrate state the surface already shows.

`saveButton.disabled = true` for the whole snackbar lifetime means the state machine cannot be re-exercised while a toast is live — replacement/stacking behaviour is unreachable, and `clearLive()`'s `close('replaced')` branch is effectively dead code. It also blurs the button when a keyboard user activates it, so focus drops to body with no focus management on either open or close (recoverable in one Tab only because the snackbar happens to be the last focusable node in the document).

`this.frame` stores either a `setTimeout` id or a `requestAnimationFrame` id, and `clearFrame()` picks the canceller from the *current* `reduceMotion.matches`. If the OS motion preference changes while a snackbar is live, the wrong canceller runs and the tick loop leaks.

`pause()` and `setRemaining()` write to the shared global `readoutTimer` with no ownership check, unlike every other cross-snackbar path, which is guarded by `live !== mine` — a hover on a closing snackbar can stamp `held` over the current one's countdown.
A snackbar that appears under a stationary pointer will not fire `mouseenter` until the pointer next moves, so the hold-on-hover guarantee has a hole at exactly the moment the surface appears.
votes.worst_defect: The snackbar is its own `role=\"status\"` live region, created fully populated and then appended, which is the pattern screen readers are least reliable at announcing — meaning the confirmation and its 6-second Undo window may never be announced at all, despite a persistent container element already existing to serve as the live region.

strengths: Real mount/unmount: the snackbar is built with createElement and torn down with removeChild — nothing is CSS-hidden — and removal is guarded by both a `transitionend` (filtered on `event.target === root` and `propertyName === 'opacity'`) and a `DURATION_EXIT + 120` timeout behind a `removed` flag, so no orphan node is possible in either direction.

Genuine generation guards: `if (live !== mine) return` in `onDismiss` and in the 900ms ack timer means a superseded snackbar can never re-enable the Save button or overwrite harness state — traced through save→undo→revert and the replaced path, and it holds.

prefers-reduced-motion actually collapses everything, including the motion CSS can't reach: the global `transition-duration: 0.001ms !important` kills the enter/exit, and `tick()` swaps rAF for a 250ms setTimeout with the remaining fraction quantized to `Math.ceil(f*10)/10`, so the JS-driven timer hairline steps instead of sweeping.

The state machine is real rather than decorative — optimistic `commit()` before acknowledgement, pending→acknowledged, rollback on undo, hover/focus pause with deadline arithmetic (`remaining = deadline - now`, `deadline = now + remaining`), Esc dismiss, and a `cssMs()` parser that correctly handles both `ms` and bare `s` token values.
defects: No focus management at all — zero `focus()` calls in the file. `saveButton.disabled = true` fires while the button holds focus after keyboard activation, so the browser drops focus to `document.body`; the user must blind-tab to Undo while the 6s countdown runs unpaused (focusin hasn't fired yet). Removing the node on Esc/Undo drops focus a second time with no restore.

Every Undo puts two snackbars in the same flex row: `close('undo')` leaves the node in the DOM for ~120ms, then `revert()` appends a second one. `.snackbar-region__column` is `display:flex` and each `.snackbar` is `width:min(520px,100%)` with default flex-shrink, so both squeeze to ~426px in the 852px column and the incoming one snaps to 520px mid-fade-in. 100% reproducible on the brief's headline interaction.

`paused` is a boolean shared by two independent pause sources. `mouseenter`+`focusin` both call `pause()` (second is a no-op), but `mouseleave` and `focusout` each call `resume()` unconditionally — so sweeping the pointer off the snackbar restarts the countdown while the Undo button still holds keyboard focus, and the surface can auto-dismiss out from under a focused control.

Undo remains interactive during its own 120ms exit transition: a second click early-returns from `close()` but still runs `options.undo()`, spawning a duplicate `revert()` snackbar that the `live !== mine` guard then orphans for its full 4s lifetime. A normal fast double-click lands inside that window.

The `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` region is injected into the DOM already populated, which NVDA and JAWS commonly fail to announce; the persistent `.snackbar-region__column` — the correct host for the live region — carries no aria attributes at all.

`clearFrame()` reads `reduceMotion.matches` at call time rather than at schedule time, so toggling the OS setting mid-countdown can call `clearTimeout()` on a `requestAnimationFrame` id — separate id spaces, so it can silently cancel an unrelated pending timeout such as `ackTimer` or the removal fallback. Also, Esc nulls `live` before the 900ms ack fires, so the guard swallows it and the readout reads `server pending` forever on a save that actually committed.
votes.worst_defect: Focus is never managed: disabling the focused Save button drops focus to document.body, and no code moves focus into the snackbar or restores it on teardown — so a keyboard user must hunt for the inline Undo (the component's entire reason for existing) while the auto-dismiss countdown runs unpaused, and loses their place again the moment the node is removed.

strengths: Accent discipline is exemplary: one hue, one appearance in the component — a 1px --accent rule under "Undo", punctuation on the single recovery affordance, never a fill. No second hue, no gradient, no glow anywhere.

Chrome is materially restrained: zero border-radius, zero box-shadow, no elevation theatre. The snackbar lifts off the page with a single hairline frame on --bg-elev, and the × is a square-linecap 16px stroke icon in a ghost target.

Emphasis is carried by weight, not size — the message holds the 16px body band at 500 while the page's display band stays on the page's own h1. This is the exact rule the bound arena surface names, and it is obeyed without exception.

Editorial page harness rather than card-soup: the field is a hairline-ruled row with a baseline-aligned 13px tracked label against a 20px value, and the state readout is a dim mono HUD line — restrained supporting detail that doesn't compete.
defects: A hairline border-inline-start on .snackbar__actions places a ~44px floating rule inside an already-bordered 480×62px object. The 16px gap had already done the separating; the rule compartmentalises a single small object and reads as a second frame nested in the first.

480px fixed width against a one-word message leaves roughly 260px of void between "Saved" and the internal divider. The bar reads half-empty and slabby, and with the divider the message cell resembles an empty input field rather than a confirmation.

The .btn--secondary underline is built with padding-block-end: 4px on the label, which lifts the "Undo" text about 3px above the × glyph's optical centre. Two adjacent actions sitting on visibly different centres is the first thing an exacting eye catches at this size.

The aria-busy progress hairline is an accent bar on an infinite 400ms scaleX loop, but the harness clears aria-busy after 120ms — it renders as a partial orange flash that never completes a third of one cycle. Decoration carrying no signal.

Snackbar padding is 24px leading against 8px trailing; even allowing the icon's optical correction, the × lands ~16px from the right edge against 24px on the left, so the bar is not quite balanced end to end.

Page-note copy ("the confirmation below the fold of your attention") is a writerly flourish in a component fixture — the visual restraint holds but the register slips into the show-don't-sell trap at sentence level.
votes.worst_defect: The vertical hairline inside the snackbar: a rule floating within an already-bordered object, doing work the 16px gap had already done. It splits a small confirmation into two compartments and — with the 260px void left by a one-word message in a fixed 480px bar — makes the message cell read as an empty field. It is the one place in an otherwise disciplined build where the chrome asserts itself instead of receding.

strengths: All three required affordances present and functional: inline Undo, a token-sourced 6000ms auto-dismiss clock, and an explicit labelled dismiss control — and undo vs dismiss are genuinely distinct outcomes (undo restores the prior value and reports 'reverted'; dismiss leaves the save standing), verifiable in the harness readout.
Genuinely optimistic: the field value is written on click before any confirmation exists, and the snackbar confirms a change that already landed rather than announcing one in progress.

Copy is exemplary for the brief — 'Saved', one word, no selling, no apology, no restatement of the saved object; the message lands one frame after the live region is in the DOM so AT announces the change, not the insertion.

Clock hold is real pause/resume with banked remaining time (not a naive full restart), wired to both pointer and focus, and onFocusOut correctly ignores relatedTarget inside the surface and bails while still hovered.
defects: release() on pointerleave has no focus-containment guard (the mirror of the hover guard in onFocusOut), so pointer-leave restarts the clock while keyboard focus is still inside the snackbar — it then auto-dismisses under the focused element and drops focus to body.

hold() early-returns unless state === 'visible', which is only set on the entrance transitionend; a pointer already inside the snackbar's rect at insertion is ignored and the full clock runs unheld with the cursor parked inside, and the later pointerleave no-ops so it never self-corrects.
The same state guard makes Undo and the dismiss X silent no-ops for ~240ms while both are fully painted and clickable — a dead-click window, not a deferred action.
Neither undo nor dismiss returns focus anywhere; teardown() removes the node while the dismiss button holds focus, sending focus to body.

Harness readout still shows 'Last outcome pending' after commit (visible on screen beside a snackbar reading 'Saved') — setOutcome is never called on commit, so the demo's instrumentation contradicts the optimistic framing.
A 120ms aria-busy progress bar precedes the snackbar — a pending affordance an optimistic save doesn't need, mildly muddying the 'already happened' read.
votes.worst_defect: The auto-dismiss hold fails in exactly the two cases the brief names: release() restarts the clock on pointerleave without checking whether keyboard focus is still inside the surface, and hold() ignores a pointer that enters during the ~240ms 'entering' state, so the snackbar can auto-dismiss with the pointer parked in it or with focus on the Undo button.

strengths: The state machine is real, not decorative: `state` is a single authoritative variable, every transition is guarded (`if (state !== "visible") return` on undo/dismiss/clock-fire, `state !== "entering"` inside the nested rAF, `state !== "leaving"` in finishLeave), and the DOM `data-state` attribute is a *reflection* of it rather than the source of truth. The surface is genuinely created via `document.createElement` in `build()` and genuinely removed via `parentNode.removeChild` in `teardown()` — nothing is CSS-hidden, and `teardown()` also clears all three timers and resets `held`, so no stale handle survives a cycle.

The auto-dismiss clock is properly pausable and resumable, with correct arithmetic: `hold()` clears the timeout and decrements `remaining` by `Date.now() - startedAt`; `release()` restarts from the true remainder. It is held by BOTH pointer (`pointerenter`/`pointerleave`) and keyboard focus (`focusin`/`focusout`), and `onFocusOut` correctly ignores focus moves *within* the snackbar (`node.contains(ev.relatedTarget)`) and refuses to release while the pointer is still inside (`node.matches(":hover")`). The `held` re-entrancy guard prevents a hover-then-focus sequence from double-decrementing. This is the part most builds get wrong and it is right here.

Entrance/exit are committed with a two-frame rAF (append → paint → set text → paint → flip to `visible`), so the transition actually fires instead of being collapsed by style batching, and every `transitionend` listener has a `setTimeout` fallback (`ENTER + 40`, `EXIT + 40`) plus an `ev.target !== node` guard so a bubbled `transitionend` from a hovered child button cannot advance the machine. Timings are read out of the token layer via `getComputedStyle` + a `ms()` parser rather than duplicated as JS literals, so the CSS and JS clocks cannot drift apart.

`prefers-reduced-motion` genuinely collapses motion rather than being a decorative block: the translate is removed from all three states, the exit transition is set to `none` AND the JS takes a separate branch (`if (isReduced()) { finishLeave(); return; }`) so it does not wait on a `transitionend` that will never fire — the classic reduced-motion hang is explicitly avoided. The harness's fake-latency delay also drops to `0` under reduced motion, and the button's infinite progress animation is stopped and pinned to `scaleX(1)`.
defects: No focus restoration on teardown — the single real keyboard bug. `onUndo()` and the dismiss path call `teardown()`, which removes the node while the just-activated Undo or × button holds focus. `document.activeElement` falls back to `<body>`, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document and the user's place is lost. Nothing captures `document.activeElement` before `commit()` or returns focus to `#save` after. Reproducible on the very first keyboard use.

No Escape handler. Explicit dismiss exists only as a mouse-or-tab-to-the-icon-button path; there is no `keydown` listener anywhere in the file. For a transient surface that a keyboard user has just tabbed into, Esc is the expected exit and it does nothing.

`hold()` early-returns unless `state === "visible"`, so hover/focus during the 200ms `entering` window is not registered. A pointer that lands on the snackbar mid-entrance never sets `held`, the full 6s clock starts anyway, and `release()` on `pointerleave` bails at `!held` — so the surface can auto-dismiss out from under a pointer that never left it. Narrow window, but it is a hole in the stated 'holds its clock as long as your pointer is inside' contract.

The `aria-live`/`role="status"` region is created and destroyed with the snackbar. Injecting a live region and populating it one rAF later is a known-fragile announcement pattern — several SR/browser pairs will not announce a region that did not exist before the mutation. A persistent, always-present region written to on commit would be the reliable construction. The one-frame delay is a thoughtful mitigation, not a fix.

Keyboard double-activation of Save is not blocked. `aria-busy="true"` sets `pointer-events: none`, which stops a second *click* but not a second Enter/Space on the already-focused button; two `setTimeout`s queue, and the second `commit()` tears down a snackbar that is one frame old. Also leaves orphaned rAF closures from the first commit that re-attach a duplicate `transitionend` handler and overwrite `enterTimer` (the leaked timer is guarded, so this degrades to harmless rather than broken — but the guard is what saves it, not the design).

`aria-labelledby` on the bare `<span id="field-value">` is inert — a generic span with no role is not a labelable element, so the association is silently dropped. The optimistic value change itself is also never announced; only the 'Saved' confirmation is.
votes.worst_defect: Focus is dropped to `<body>` whenever the snackbar is torn down: `onUndo()` and the dismiss path remove the node while the activated button still has focus, and no `document.activeElement` is captured before `commit()` or restored to `#save` afterward — so a keyboard user who tabs to Undo and presses Enter loses their tab position on first use. The lens's other three checks (real state machine, real DOM add/remove, genuine reduced-motion collapse) all pass cleanly; this is the one that does not.

strengths: Genuinely ink-on-paper: zero radius, hairline 1px rules, no shadow, no glow, no gradient, no card nesting. The snackbar is a bordered rectangle on an elevated ground and nothing more — the chrome recedes exactly as DESIGN.md asks.

Emphasis is carried by weight and colour, never display size. The h1 token (96px) is deliberately left unused; the page title caps at 56px at weight 500, and inside the snackbar the message (16 regular white), Undo (16 medium accent), and dismiss (16px icon at fg-dim) separate purely by role.

The countdown is a 1px accent hairline riding the snackbar's existing bottom border rather than an added progress bar — the most restrained possible expression of the auto-dismiss mechanic, and it costs zero new geometry.

One coherent quiet register: mono 13px uppercase tracked at fg-dim for the eyebrow, the record label, and the harness readout, so all instrumentation reads as the same recessive layer. Copy is plain and concrete throughout ("Visibility set to Public.", "holds an Undo for six seconds, and gets out of the way") — no persuasion, no adjectives.
defects: Spacing rhythm: the snackbar is anchored to the viewport inset (left/bottom 32px) while every other element sits in a 720px centred column starting at x=280. On the rendered 1280px page its left edge answers to nothing — it is the only element off the page's grid.

Declared width does not govern the rendered width. No `box-sizing: border-box` reset exists in the file, so `width: min(var(--snackbar-max, 460px), 100%)` plus 24+16px padding and two hairlines renders at 502px — measured x=32→534. The token is decorative rather than load-bearing.

Accent economy slips on one 460px component: accent on the Undo label, accent on a ~400px full-bleed countdown rule, accent on the focus ring. In the 2× crop the orange rule is optically louder than the confirmation message it exists to serve.

Token misuse as craft tell: `--radius-flat` (0px) is used as the zero for `margin` on body/title/lede/message and for `padding` on the icon button. A radius token standing in for a spacing zero is literal-avoidance, not system discipline.

The ghost hover presses to `--color-bg` (#050505), darker than the snackbar's own `--color-bg-elev` surface — hovering Undo punches a hole through the elevated bar rather than lifting it. The contrast reasoning in the comment is sound; the resulting visual is crude.

The meter overlays the border at `bottom: -1px, left/right: -1px`, so mid-countdown the bottom edge reads orange for 88% of its run and grey for the rest — visible in the crop as a colour break partway along one edge, which scans as an artifact rather than a deliberate rule.
votes.worst_defect: The snackbar is spatially unmoored: pinned to the viewport at 32px while the whole page lives in a 720px centred column at x=280, and rendering 502px wide instead of the 460px its own token declares because the file never sets `box-sizing: border-box`. On a wide screen it reads as a floating fragment rather than part of the composition.

strengths: All three required affordances exist and are genuinely distinct: inline Undo restores the prior value and confirms with its own short-lived "Change reverted." notice, the × (plus Escape) only removes the surface and leaves the new value committed, and a 6s rAF countdown auto-dismisses with a visible hairline meter.

Truly optimistic: the record mutates on click before any confirmation, with no fake latency or pending/spinner state, and the copy ("Visibility set to Public.") states the outcome with no selling, apology, or "successfully".

The clock is held for both pointer (pointerenter/leave) and keyboard focus (focusin/focusout with a relatedTarget containment check), and additionally while the tab is hidden — remaining time is tracked from performance.now() deltas, so it survives rAF throttling rather than drifting.

State machine is tidy under repeat use: a second save tears down the standing snackbar before presenting, teardown cancels both the rAF and the exit timer, and reduced motion drops the meter node entirely instead of animating a hidden element.
defects: Pause is a boolean, not a counter, so "held while focus is inside" is defeatable: tab to Undo, then move the pointer over the snackbar and off again — pointerleave calls resume() while focus is still on Undo, and the auto-dismiss can then remove the element the keyboard user is standing on. Same class of bug on the visibilitychange path: returning to the tab resumes unconditionally even with the pointer or focus still inside.

Undo's deferred `setTimeout(present(revertNotice()), EXIT_MS+60)` is never cancelled. Press Save within ~180ms of Undo and the fresh confirmation is torn down and replaced by "Change reverted." — the snackbar then contradicts the record, which now shows the newly saved value.

Focus is never returned to the Save button when the snackbar is removed. Dismissing with the keyboard (× or Escape) or auto-dismissing while a snackbar button is focused drops focus to <body>, so the keyboard user loses their place after every save cycle.

The message restates the object already on screen — the record row directly above reads VISIBILITY / Public, and the snackbar says "Visibility set to Public." A confirmation for a change the user can already see wants to be shorter ("Saved."/"Visibility updated.").

Dead `.record__value[data-pending="true"]` rule with a color transition is declared but nothing ever sets that attribute — a pending state that was designed and then not wired, left in the shipped CSS.

The snackbar's interactive controls live inside a persistent `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` region, so "Undo" and "Dismiss" are read out as part of the announcement rather than presented as reachable controls; the announcement is also the only signal that a time-limited action exists.

strengths: Real DOM lifecycle, not CSS visibility theatre: nodes are createElement'd, appendChild'd (l.599) and removeChild'd (l.481), with a forced reflow (`void snack.node.offsetWidth`, l.601) so the entrance transition genuinely runs.

The timer is a real rAF delta accumulator (`tick`, l.501-514) rather than setInterval — pause/resume adjusts `last` instead of guessing elapsed time, the meter and the readout are driven from the same `remaining` value, and both `rafId` and `exitTimer` are cancelled in `teardown`.

prefers-reduced-motion genuinely collapses the motion: transitions are zeroed AND the countdown meter element is never constructed (l.577-584) rather than hidden, and `build()` re-evaluates `reduced.matches` per call so a mid-session OS toggle is respected.

Accessibility fundamentals are right: a persistent live region outside the churn (role=status + aria-atomic, l.425), aria-label on the icon-only close, aria-hidden/focusable=false on the SVG, focus-visible rings, 44px minimum targets, and pointer-events:none on the fixed region so it never blankets the page.

Pause bookkeeping is a single boolean shared by hover, focus and tab-visibility. `pointerleave` resumes unconditionally (l.587), so moving the mouse off while Undo holds keyboard focus restarts the countdown and lets auto-dismiss yank a focused control; `focusout` and `visibilitychange` have the mirror problem.
`.record__value[data-pending="true"]` (l.174-176) is dead CSS — nothing ever sets `data-pending`, so the pending affordance is styling for a state the machine does not model.
`present()` hard-removes a live snackbar with no exit transition when a second save arrives (l.597), bypassing the exit path that exists for every other close route.

The undo closure reads module-level `previousValue` (l.612) instead of capturing it per-snack; correct only by the accident of single-slot presentation, and it is the mechanism by which defect #2 produces a stale message.

The component speaks the page's own vocabulary instead of inventing chrome: the vertical `--rule-hairline` divider between message and actions is the same primitive as the field row's `border-block`. Flat `--color-bg-elev` plane, one hairline border, zero border-radius, zero box-shadow, no elevation trickery, no nested cards. The chrome genuinely recedes.

Emphasis is carried by weight and color, never by display size. Component text stays entirely in the 13/16px band (message 16/500 white, actions 16/500, close label sr-only), while the page's 96px title is confined to the harness. The ladder eyebrow-13-mono-dim → label-13-uppercase-dim → body-16 → lead-20-muted → title-96 is coherent and uses only three greys.

Detail craft in the small marks: the dismiss glyph is a hand-authored 1.25-stroke, square-linecap X rather than a rounded icon-library default; the focus ring is monochrome white 2px/2px offset; hover states exist on every interactive element and are all monochrome (border-color, fg lift, `--color-bg-card` wash). A 4× jump converts the accent from punctuation into a solid orange bar under the word — the one place the component's restraint breaks — and it does so by borrowing a *spacing* token as a stroke weight, which is a token-semantics violation in a file that otherwise declares `--rule-hairline` for exactly this purpose.

Alignment failure against the composition: the snackbar is `min(100% - 32px, 34rem)` centred on the viewport (543px, edges at x≈368 and x≈911 in the capture) while the content column is 44rem at x≈288–992. Neither edge, nor the internal divider, relates to any line in the page. In an editorial hairline system where every other element sits on a shared column, the confirmation reads as an unrelated object floating in the lower frame.

Uneven optical rhythm inside the action cluster: `.snackbar__actions` sets an 8px gap and 8px inline padding, but `.btn` contributes 24px inline padding, so the measured runs are divider→"Undo" ≈35px and "Undo"→X ≈54px. The close glyph floats away from the label it belongs with, and its 44px-wide full-bleed hover slab sits only 8px off the right hairline.

The lede narrates its own implementation instead of showing it: "The confirmation carries the only path back, so its clock holds while a pointer or keyboard focus is inside it" is spec documentation set at 20px lead across three lines in the display position. Restrained systems demonstrate the hover-hold; they do not annotate it above the fold.

Page furniture outshouts the subject. The 96px `--type-h1` title plus a persistent mono `state / clock / last outcome` readout row occupy the majority of the frame, while the artifact under test is the smallest, lowest element. The readout is defensible as state-machine instrumentation, but combined with the display title it inverts the hierarchy of what the page is for.

Minor literal leakage in a file whose stated discipline is `var(--token, fallback)` everywhere: `opacity: 0.72` on the loading label, `stroke-width="1.25"` on the icon, `z-index: 10`, and the reduced-motion exit guard hardcoded as `60` in JS alongside tokenised durations.
votes.worst_defect: The hover state escalates the accent underline from 1px to 4px (via `--space-xs`, a spacing token used as a stroke weight) — the single moment the accent stops being punctuation and becomes a bar, in the one component the brief was about.

strengths: All three required affordances exist and behave distinctly: inline Undo (reverts `committed`/`pending` and writes "Change reverted…"), a 6s auto-dismiss, and an explicit × dismiss with an sr-only "Dismiss" label plus Escape — undo terminates in S.REVERTED, dismiss/timeout in S.DISMISSED with a distinct "Change kept…" outcome, so the two paths are genuinely different results, not two ways to close a bar.

The hold-the-clock requirement is implemented properly, not gestured at: pause on `pointerenter`/`focusin` banks the remaining time via `startedAt`, and `resume()` re-checks BOTH `:hover` and `root.contains(document.activeElement)` before restarting — so pointer-out-while-focused (and focus-out-while-hovered) correctly stays held, the case most implementations get wrong.
Copy is exactly on brief: the message is the single word "Saved" — states what happened, no selling, no apology, no restatement of the saved object or its new value.

The save is genuinely optimistic (the field flips to Public on click, before the simulated round trip), and the state machine is defensive in the right places: `transitionend` guarded by a 400ms fallback timer, `inert` + `disabled` applied on leave so a late click can't re-enter the machine, focus read before inerting and returned to the Save button, and a second save supersedes the first with its callbacks nulled so the stale bar can't overwrite the new outcome.
defects: The pause guard requires `state === S.VISIBLE`, but the clock only starts at the END of the ~200ms entrance. A pointerenter or focusin during ENTERING is dropped as a no-op, and since no second pointerenter fires for a stationary cursor, `startClock(6000)` then runs unpaused with the pointer sitting inside the surface — the exact failure the hold requirement exists to prevent, just inside a narrow window.

The fixture's field copy is wrong about what happened after the save: it renders "Public — pending change: Private", so the page simultaneously claims the change committed and that an opposite change is still pending. Nothing is pending; it's the swapped variable rendered as a state label.

The Save button enters a `is-loading` / `disabled` / `cursor: progress` state for 600ms while the snackbar already says "Saved" — a pending-round-trip affordance bolted onto a flow whose premise is that the UI does not wait for the round trip.

Superseding save mounts the new bar before the old one finishes leaving, so two snackbars occupy the same fixed bottom-center slot for ~200ms, and the superseded bar writes "superseded" into the last-outcome readout after the replacement is already up.

The polite live region announces only "Saved" — a screen-reader user is told the outcome but not that a time-limited Undo exists; the `aria-label="Save confirmation"` on the group is only reachable if they navigate into it before the 6s clock expires.
votes.worst_defect: Hover/focus arriving during the ~200ms entrance is silently dropped (pause() returns early unless state is VISIBLE), so the auto-dismiss clock can run its full 6s with the pointer resting inside the surface.

strengths: Genuinely real state machine: six named states with entry guards on every transition (`activateUndo`/`activateDismiss`/`activateTimeout` all bail unless `state === VISIBLE`), and the surface is truly `appendChild`'d on mount and `removeChild`'d on unmount — never CSS-hidden. Transient state is driven by transitionend with a `once()` helper that carries a `MOTION_GUARD_MS` fallback timer and self-removes, so a swallowed transitionend cannot strand the node.

Focus handling is deliberate and correct in the hard spot: `leave()` reads `root.contains(document.activeElement)` BEFORE setting `inert` (with a comment explaining that inert blurs its subtree), then restores focus to `returnFocusTo`. The exit path also disables both buttons and sets `pointer-events:none`, so a late click cannot re-enter the machine.

The auto-dismiss clock is a real accumulating timer, not a naive setTimeout: `pause()` banks `remaining` and zeroes `startedAt`, `resume()` re-guards against `:hover` and `contains(document.activeElement)` before restarting, and `focusout` ignores relatedTarget still inside the bar. Escape is wired, and the readout proves the clock live (5.5s in the screenshot).

Supersede is handled explicitly and correctly: a second Save nulls the old bar's `onUndo`/`onDismiss` so it cannot write a stale outcome over the new one, and `unmount()` guards `if (current === this)` so the outgoing bar's async unmount does not clobber the incoming bar's state readout. The undo value swap (`committed`/`pending`) round-trips exactly.
defects: Keyboard focus is dropped on every keyboard-initiated save. `commitSave` sets `saveBtn.disabled = true` for ROUND_TRIP_MS (600ms) while the button still holds focus — disabling a focused element blurs it, so `document.activeElement` falls to `<body>`. The button re-enables but focus is never restored, so a keyboard user loses their tab position on first use. `aria-busy` is already set; the disable is redundant and is what breaks it.

The same 600ms window poisons the focus-return contract: if the bar is dismissed or undone before the round trip finishes, `returnFocusTo.focus()` targets a still-disabled button and is a no-op, silently dropping focus to body instead of back to Save.

Escape is bound on the snackbar root only, so explicit keyboard dismiss requires first tabbing into the bar. There is no document-level Escape handler; a keyboard user who never tabs in has no keyboard dismiss path at all.

Undo, Escape, and dismiss are silently inert during the ~230ms ENTERING window (double rAF + 200ms transition) because every activator requires `state === VISIBLE`. Input in that window is dropped with no queueing.

Mount is gated on `requestAnimationFrame`, which is throttled in a background tab: saving and immediately switching tabs leaves the node in the DOM at `opacity:0` with no auto-dismiss timer armed until the tab is refocused. Self-heals, but the surface is present-and-invisible in the meantime.

State-model wart: the undo path sets `state = REVERTED` at the START of the exit animation rather than LEAVING, so LEAVING is never entered for undo and the readout reports a terminal state while motion is still running. Also `var VALUES = ["Private", "Public"]` is dead code.
votes.worst_defect: Disabling the focused Save button for the 600ms simulated round trip blurs it to `<body>`, so every keyboard-initiated save loses focus position — and any dismiss/undo inside that window has its `returnFocusTo.focus()` silently no-op against a disabled element.

strengths: Genuinely editorial construction: zero radius, zero shadow, zero glow, no gradient anywhere — the snackbar is one square hairline-framed bar segmented by internal 1px rules into message | Undo | ×, rather than a floating pill with a button parked inside it. No card-soup, no nested surface, and it is anchored to the same content-column width as the page rather than centre-floating, so it reads as part of the page grid instead of an overlay from another design system.

Accent discipline is exact. #ed4609 appears on exactly one thing in the rendered state — the word "Undo" — plus ::selection. No accent fill, no second hue, no accent on the timer, the border, or the primary button. The undo is the loudest thing in the component and it is loud only because it is the only coloured thing.

Hierarchy is carried by weight, colour and register, never by display size. Snackbar message sits at body 16/400 in --color-fg; the dismiss is --color-fg-muted and recedes; all metadata (eyebrow, CURRENT label, readout) is 13px mono with 0.08em tracking, forming one consistent secondary register. Nothing is enlarged to be emphatic.

Quiet load-bearing detail rather than decoration: the value dims to --color-fg-muted for 600ms while the optimistic write settles and resolves to white; the × is a 16px currentColor stroke with square linecap matching the zero-radius language; inner focus rings use a negative offset so they inset instead of breaking the bar's edge. Copy is deadpan and unexclaimed ("Visibility set to Public.").
defects: The depleting timer is the one visible craft failure. It is --rule-strong (2px) laid over a 1px --color-line-strong frame at the bottom edge, so the box carries two different stroke weights on the same edge, and because it scales from the left it renders — as in the screenshot — as a bottom border that stops partway across (~x=637) with a gap to the right. At a glance it reads as a rendering artefact or a broken border, not as remaining time. A hairline at --rule-hairline inset above the frame, or a top-edge rule, would have said the same thing without damaging the box.

The snackbar's frame is --color-line-strong (#545454) while every other rule on the page is --color-line (#363636), making the component's own chrome the brightest hairline on the surface. Defensible for an overlay, but it is the chrome asserting rather than receding.

Four separate stroke elements on one 480px object — outer frame, two internal dividers, timer bar — is mild over-articulation for a transient confirmation. The × cell in particular is fenced off by its own rule for a control that is already the quietest thing in the bar.

The demo harness explains rather than shows: a four-line hint paragraph narrating pause-on-hover, undo, and escape, plus a live "state / remaining" readout that duplicates what the timer bar already encodes. Instrumentation is honest for a fixture, but the prose block is the one place the page tells instead of demonstrating.

Two off-scale spacing values — calc(--space-xxl * 1.5) = 72px and calc(--space-xxl * 3) = 144px — sit outside the declared 4/8/16/24/32/48 ladder. Visually fine, but it breaks the claim that every value is a token.
Minor authoring impurity: .sr-only borrows --rule-hairline for its 1px clip dimensions, which is token reuse where the semantics don't hold.
votes.worst_defect: The auto-dismiss timer is a 2px bar overlaid on the snackbar's 1px bottom border, so the box shows two stroke weights on one edge and — mid-countdown — reads as a bottom border that simply stops partway across. It is the only element on an otherwise immaculately restrained component that looks like a mistake rather than a decision.

strengths: All three required affordances exist and behave distinctly: inline Undo (restores the previous value and raises its own shorter 3.2s "Reverted to Private." confirmation with no further undo), a 6s auto-dismiss driven by a rAF clock with a visible depleting hairline, and an explicit dismiss (X button with aria-label plus Escape). Dismiss is silent and leaves the change applied; Undo reverts state and confirms — genuinely different outcomes, not two spellings of "close".

The auto-dismiss hold is the sub-requirement most builds get wrong, and this one gets the interlock right. `pointerenter`/`focusin` both pause; `pointerleave` and `focusout` both route through `maybeResume()`, which re-checks BOTH `hovered` and `node.contains(document.activeElement)` before resuming, and `focusout` early-returns when `relatedTarget` is still inside. Hover-then-tab-in-then-unhover correctly stays paused. Window blur also leaves it paused because activeElement survives.

Optimistic semantics are actually modeled, not just asserted: `commit()` writes the new value to the DOM immediately, marks it `data-pending` for 600ms while "the request settles," and raises the confirmation at once. The page copy and the state readout (state / remaining) make the machine legible without faking a loading gate.

Copy is restrained and factual — "Visibility set to Public." / "Reverted to Private." State what happened, no apology, no selling, no exclamation, no "Success!" wrapper. Reduced-motion is honored end-to-end (exit duration collapses to 0), and every value is `var(--token, fallback)` against the exact DESIGN.md numbers with no external requests.
defects: Keyboard focus is dropped on the Undo path. `dismiss()` restores focus to the Save button when focus was inside the snackbar, but clicking Undo never calls `dismiss()` — `onUndo` goes straight to `show()`, whose `clearImmediately()` + `while (region.firstChild) removeChild` tears out the focused Undo button with no focus restore. A keyboard user who tabs to Undo and presses Enter lands on `<body>`. That is the single most likely keyboard path through this component.

Explicit dismiss does not disarm Undo. `dismiss()` sets `current = null` and starts a 200ms exit, but the node stays in the DOM with `pointer-events: auto` and the Undo listener live. A click in the Undo cell within that 200ms window (after pressing X, or after Escape) still fires `onUndo` and reverts the save — the two outcomes the brief wants kept distinct can collide.

The polite live region announces only the message text ("Visibility set to Public."). It never signals that a time-limited Undo exists, so a screen-reader user is given the confirmation but not the affordance, and the countdown that governs it is invisible to them. The visible snackbar itself carries no role, so nothing associates the announcement with the buttons.

Escape is bound globally on `document` and fires whenever `current` is truthy, regardless of where focus is. A non-modal snackbar hijacking Escape from anywhere on the page is more aggressive than the pattern warrants; scoping it to focus-within (or focus-within plus a documented global) would be the correct behavior.

The message half-restates what the row already shows. The setting is labeled "Project visibility" and the row reads "CURRENT Public" two inches above; the snackbar then says "Visibility set to Public." It is defensible as a state readback, but it is the object restated rather than purely the event.

Minor: a stale `exitTimer` from a superseded snackbar is never cleared. `clearImmediately()` only touches `current`, and a node already in the `leaving` phase is not `current`, so its 200ms timer survives the sweep and can later fire `setReadout("idle", null)` while a second snackbar is mid-exit. Harness-readout only, no user-facing effect.
votes.worst_defect: Clicking Undo destroys the focused button without restoring focus — the `onUndo` path bypasses `dismiss()` and its focus-return, so a keyboard user who activates Undo is stranded on `<body>`. Dismiss handles this correctly; undo, the more important path, does not.

strengths: State machine is genuinely real, not decorative: rAF-driven countdown with preserved `remaining` across pause/resume — live-measured 5.9s→5.4s ticking, then held at 5.4s across 500ms while focus was inside. Pause fires on both `pointerenter` and `focusin`, and `maybeResume()` correctly refuses to resume while either hover or focus is still held.

The surface is truly added to and removed from the DOM. `.snackbar` count measured 0 → 1 → 0 across auto-dismiss, Escape, and close-button paths; `removeNode()` runs after the exit delay, and `show()` sweeps `region.firstChild` so only one node can ever exist. No CSS-hidden zombie.

prefers-reduced-motion genuinely collapses on BOTH sides. CSS: measured `transitionDuration: 1e-06s` and the snackbar already at `opacity: 1` on first paint. JS: `var exit = reduceMotion.matches ? 0 : EXIT_MS` reads `.matches` live at dismiss time, so the removal isn't stuck behind a 200ms wait for a transition that never runs.

Concurrency and lifecycle edges are handled, verified live: rapid triple Save and a dismiss-immediately-followed-by-save both end with exactly one snackbar and a correct `remaining`; the departing entry's `exitTimer` is guarded by `if (!current)` so it can't stomp the new one's readout. Zero console/page errors on every path exercised.
defects: CONFIRMED, primary path: activating Undo drops focus to `document.body`. `options.onUndo()` calls `show()` → `clearImmediately()` → `removeNode()`, synchronously removing the node containing the just-activated button. `dismiss()` implements focus restoration (`hadFocus → saveButton.focus()`) but this path does not, so a keyboard user loses their tab position on the single most important control in the brief (WCAG 2.4.3). Measured `document.activeElement === body` in both motion modes.

The depleting hairline is rAF-driven (`--snackbar-progress` set every frame in `tick()`) with no `reduceMotion.matches` check, so it keeps animating continuously under prefers-reduced-motion while every other motion in the file correctly collapses. Defensible as an informational countdown, but it is the one motion the reduced-motion handling misses.

The `role="status"` announcement is the bare message ("Visibility set to Public.") — it never mentions that an Undo exists or that the notice will self-dismiss. The Undo button is reachable only by Tab and announces as a context-free "Undo". The brief's headline affordance is functionally opaque to a screen-reader user until they happen to tab into it.

During the ~200ms `leaving` phase the node stays in the DOM with `pointer-events: auto` and two still-focusable buttons at `opacity: 0`. Narrow window, but a Tab or click landing there hits an invisible departing control; `inert` or a `tabindex`/`pointer-events` flip on `data-phase="leaving"` would close it.

`saveButton` is never disabled during the 600ms optimistic window even though `.btn[disabled]` styling is authored. Behavior stays correct under rapid clicks (verified), so this is unused CSS plus a missed affordance rather than a functional break.
votes.worst_defect: Activating Undo destroys keyboard focus — `show()`/`clearImmediately()` removes the focused button's node from the DOM with no focus restoration, so `document.activeElement` falls to `body` (confirmed live in both motion modes). The author demonstrably knew to handle this, since `dismiss()` restores focus to the Save button; the branch was simply missed on the one path the brief cares most about.

strengths: Hierarchy inside the component is carried by weight and colour, never size — 16px/400 white message against a 13px/500 accent "Undo" — which is exactly the arena binding's rule. Radius 0 throughout, no shadow, no glow, no elevation trickery, one hue; the bar separates from the page on bg-elev + a single hairline and nothing else.

Spacing is grouped rather than uniform: 16px between message and action cluster, 4px inside it, so the two controls read as one unit at a glance. Bar padding is deliberately asymmetric (24px left, 8px right) with the 44px tap box supplying the optical right inset — that's an exacting call, not sloppiness.

The single piece of decoration is load-bearing and honest. The countdown hairline IS the undo window, hover/focus pauses it, and under prefers-reduced-motion the element is never built at all rather than freezing as a static bar that would lie about remaining time.

A second, free axis of hierarchy: mono is reserved for machine values (the ACCOUNT eyebrow, the "Private" state) while prose stays in the sans body band. Costs nothing visually and makes the changed value legible without bolding or colouring it.
defects: The snackbar is anchored to the viewport gutter (left: 24px) while the page content column begins at ~304px, so its left edge, the hairline rules, and the h1 all start at different x positions. In the render it floats unmoored in the lower-left corner of an otherwise centred editorial page — the one visible break in the layout's rhythm.

The accent is spent twice inside one 460px component: the Undo label and a ~400px countdown rail. In the screenshot that rail is the largest and most saturated mass of colour on the entire page, which pressures the "punctuation, not fill" rule — a hairline in --line-strong would have carried the same information without out-shouting everything above it.

Eyebrow treatment (uppercase + 0.08em --tracking-label) is applied to every button, so the white "SAVE CHANGE" slab becomes the loudest ink on the page while the actual setting value sits in muted grey. The .btn--ghost variant that would have kept chrome quieter is fully authored and never used.

The demo page narrates its own interaction in three explainer lines ("The hairline shows what is left of the window", "Hover or focus holds the countdown"). Deadpan in voice, but it is telling where the brief's standard is showing — the component already demonstrates all three.

CSS comments editorialise about their own restraint — "the accent is punctuation here, never a fill", "the only decoration here, and it is load-bearing". Selling in the source of an artifact whose whole standard is not selling.

Interior air is adequate rather than generous: an 8px bar pad plus 8px message padding-block yields ~15px of optical space above and below a single line of 16px text, so the bar reads slightly compressed against the openness of the page it sits under.
votes.worst_defect: The snackbar is pinned to the viewport gutter instead of the page's content column, so its left edge aligns with nothing on the page — unlike the accent-rail loudness, which is at least a defensible judgment call, this one has no reading in which it is deliberate.

strengths: Genuinely optimistic and genuinely three-affordance: the value flips before the snackbar is built, Undo reverts and confirms with distinct terse copy, and the X (plus Escape) dismisses while leaving the change standing — dismiss and undo are unambiguously different outcomes.

The auto-dismiss clock and the countdown hairline are driven from the same `--snackbar-dwell` custom property (`dwellOf()` reads the computed value off the element), so the visible progress bar cannot lie about the real timeout — and the terse 3600ms variant reroutes both at once.

Pause/resume arithmetic is correct across repeated cycles: `hold()` subtracts elapsed from `remaining` and pauses `animation-play-state`, `run()` re-arms from the remainder and un-pauses, so the bar and the timer stay in step. `focusout` correctly ignores relatedTarget still inside the surface, so tabbing Undo -> Dismiss does not restart the clock.

Copy states what happened without selling or apologising ("Visibility set to Private." / "Visibility restored to Public."), and focus is returned to the Save button when a snackbar holding focus is torn down.
defects: Hover-hold and focus-hold share one latch instead of composing: `mouseleave` calls `entry.run()` unconditionally, so moving the pointer away while keyboard focus is still on the Undo button resumes the countdown — and `focusout` resumes it while the pointer is still inside the surface. The brief requires the clock held while pointer OR focus is inside.

No initial-hover check on append (`el.matches(':hover')` or equivalent): a snackbar that renders underneath an already-stationary cursor never receives `mouseenter`, so it counts down and disappears with the pointer sitting on it.

Undo survives the undo window: `teardown()` adds `.snackbar--leaving` and only removes the node on `animationend`, leaving the button clickable with `pointer-events: auto` for the ~120ms fade, so a late click reverts the change after expiry.
The Escape handler is bound globally to `document` and fires on any keypress anywhere while a snackbar exists, with no scoping to the surface or check for a competing dismissible layer.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the countdown hairline is omitted entirely while the JS timeout still runs, so those users get an auto-dismiss with no indication of how much undo window remains — defensible, but it removes the one signal that makes the timeout legible.
Message copy names "Visibility", duplicating both the page H1 and the value already rendered in the row immediately above the snackbar — mild restatement of the saved object.
votes.worst_defect: Hover-hold and focus-hold are a single shared latch rather than an OR of two states, so `mouseleave` resumes the auto-dismiss countdown while keyboard focus is still inside the snackbar (and `focusout` resumes it while the pointer is still inside) — a direct miss on the one behavior the brief calls out by name.

strengths: Genuinely real lifecycle: every showing constructs a fresh node and teardown calls removeChild — nothing is CSS-hidden. The persistent empty #snackbar-region is the correct pre-registered aria-live shell, not a hidden snackbar.

Reduced motion is handled at both layers: the countdown hairline is never constructed when reduced.matches (rather than rendering a bar that snaps to zero), and auto-dismiss runs on setTimeout rather than animationend, so collapsing animations to 0.001ms cannot strand the surface on screen. reduced.matches is re-read per show(), so a mid-session preference change is picked up.

The animationend handler explicitly filters event.target !== el because the 6000ms countdown fill's own animationend bubbles to the snackbar — exactly the bug that would otherwise tear the surface down early — backed by a done latch and a 400ms fallback timer.

Pause/resume does real time bookkeeping (entry.remaining decremented by elapsed, timeout re-armed with the remainder) and the CSS bar is paused in lockstep via animation-play-state; both read the same --snackbar-dwell token, so the .snackbar--terse 3600ms override drives JS and CSS identically. Focus restores to the Save button on teardown, Escape is wired, and re-entrancy is safe (teardown nulls current first, so double-dismiss is a no-op).
defects: Hold/resume is not reference-counted: mouseleave and focusout each call entry.run() unconditionally, so hovering then tabbing out (or focusing Undo then moving the mouse off) resumes the countdown while the other hold is still active — the snackbar can auto-dismiss out from under a focused Undo button, breaking the page's own stated 'hover or focus holds the countdown' contract.

Transient double-snackbar: teardown(entry,false) nulls `current` immediately but leaves the node in the DOM for ~120ms, so a show() inside that window (Escape/Dismiss then click Save) skips the `if (current)` force-removal and stacks two snackbars in the bottom-anchored region; the first teardown's deferred saveBtn.focus() then also fires after the new surface has mounted.

Interactive controls (Undo, Dismiss) live inside role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true", so they are announced as part of the status string, and nothing informs a keyboard/AT user that Undo exists or that the window expires — 6s to discover and Tab there is thin, even though focusin extends it once reached.
The 400ms teardown safety timeout is a hardcoded literal rather than derived from --motion-duration-slow, so it silently decouples if the motion tokens change.
No touch equivalent of hover-pause: on a touch device the undo window is a hard 6s with no way to extend it short of tabbing to a control.
votes.worst_defect: Hold/resume is not reference-counted — mouseleave and focusout both unconditionally restart the dwell timer, so a hover-then-tab-out (or focus-then-mouse-off) sequence resumes the countdown while the surface is still hovered or still holds focus, letting the snackbar auto-dismiss out from under a focused Undo button and violating the interaction contract the page itself states.

strengths: Accent discipline is the best thing here and it is a real idea, not compliance: #ed4609 appears exactly once in the entire document, as a 1px text-decoration-color under "Undo" — the one reversible action. No fill, no pill, no second hue, no glow, no gradient. That is 'punctuation, not fill' executed literally.

Chrome genuinely recedes: border-radius explicitly 0, zero box-shadow anywhere, elevation carried by #141414 on #050505 plus a single --color-line hairline. The internal divider between statement and controls reuses the same hairline vocabulary as the field-list rules, so the component reads as native to the page rather than a component-library import dropped on top.

Emphasis is carried by weight and colour, never by size — the page title sits at --type-h3 (27px) rather than h2/h1, the snackbar message and "Undo" are the same 16px body with only weight and the accent underline separating them, and the whole page uses four type sizes. The dismiss affordance is a 1.5-stroke currentColor X at --icon-sm on a muted ghost, which is the correct amount of nothing.

Copy restraint holds where it matters most: "Saved" — one word, unexclaimed, no checkmark icon, no "Your changes have been saved successfully." The terminal ledger line ("Last change kept." / "Last change reverted.") is deadpan and sits in dim mono at --type-label so it recedes rather than competing.
defects: Two contradictory status statements are on screen simultaneously in the delivered render: the trigger reads "Saving…" while the snackbar reads "Saved". Worse, the loading state strips the primary button's white fill for a hollow --color-line-strong outline, so the page's strongest element visually collapses at the exact moment the confirmation appears — the hierarchy inverts mid-flight. An optimistic save's whole premise is that the trigger does NOT enter a pending state; this is redundant chrome that does not recede and it undercuts the very confirmation it accompanies.

The .snackbar__actions divider is align-self:stretch inside padding-block:var(--space-xs), leaving the hairline inset exactly 4px from the top and bottom borders. At this scale that reads as a near-miss rather than a decision — a rule should either run full-bleed to the borders or be clearly inset by a real step on the scale. As rendered it gives the snackbar a faint two-cell/table look instead of a clean editorial division.

The snackbar is centred at 480px against a 688px content column, so it shares no edge with the page's only structural grid. In a system whose whole layout argument is hairline rules and a measure, the confirmation floats free of the column it is confirming a change to. Defensible by snackbar convention, but it is the one element on the page that answers to nothing.

The lede — "The confirmation carries the way back." — is a writerly flourish about the component rather than plain instruction. It is not salesy, but it is the copy admiring itself, which the surface binding's "deadpan" register does not have room for.

Optical asymmetry at the snackbar's ends: 24px from the left border to "Saved" versus ~18px from the X's edge to the right border (4px end padding plus the ghost button's own 8px inset inside a 44px target). Partly justified as icon compensation, but the right end reads slightly tight against the border in the render.

One bare visual literal survives in component CSS despite the file's own comment claiming tokens are the only place literals are permitted: max-width:60ch on .page__lede. Trivial, and ch is a defensible measure unit, but the file states a stricter rule than it keeps.
votes.worst_defect: The primary button hollows out and reads "Saving…" at the same moment the snackbar reads "Saved" — two competing status surfaces saying opposite things in one view, with the page's strongest element losing its fill and pulling emphasis away from the confirmation. It is the one thing in the delivered screenshot a designer would flag on sight, and it is a restraint failure: a pending state that an optimistic save should not have shown at all.

strengths: All three required affordances exist and behave sanely: inline Undo, a 6000ms auto-dismiss driven off a --snackbar-dwell token, and an explicit dismiss (× button with aria-label plus an Escape handler).

Undo and dismiss are genuinely distinct outcomes, not two paths to the same end — undo restores previousValue, cancels the in-flight save, and writes 'Last change reverted.'; dismiss and auto-dismiss leave the change and write 'Last change kept.'
Copy is exemplary for the lens: 'Saved' alone — no selling, no apology, no restatement of the saved object; the ledger differentiates outcomes in the same plain register.

The clock is implemented with real elapsed-time accounting (remaining/resumeAt) rather than a naive restart, plus a post-entrance race check that pauses immediately if a pointer or focus arrived during the 200ms enter animation, and a data-cancelled token so a replaced surface never reaches a terminal state.
defects: Asymmetric clock guard: `mouseleave` calls `resume()` unconditionally while `onFocusOut` correctly checks `:hover` first. Hover in → tab to Undo → move the pointer away restarts the 6s clock with keyboard focus still inside, and the surface then deletes itself out from under the focused control. Directly violates the 'held while pointer OR keyboard focus is inside' requirement.

Dismiss, Undo, and Escape all guard on `state() !== 'visible'`, but the snackbar sits in `entering` for the full 200ms enter animation. Both controls are mounted, visible, and focusable during that window yet are silent no-ops.

The optimistic framing contradicts itself on screen: the snackbar asserts 'Saved' while the trigger simultaneously reads 'Saving…' for 900ms (visible in after-save.png). A confirmation of a change that already happened should not sit beside a control saying it hasn't.
No focus restoration — `inertize()` sets `inert` on a surface that may contain focus (auto-dismiss or undo), dropping focus to <body> with nothing returning it to the Save trigger.

The simulated flight has no failure path: `settleFlight` always succeeds, so the optimistic commit can never be rolled back by the server, only by the user. Not required by the brief, but it leaves the 'optimistic' half of the pattern unexercised.
`dwellMs()` uses `parseFloat` on the raw token value, so a perfectly reasonable token edit to `6s` would silently yield a 6ms dwell rather than 6000ms.
votes.worst_defect: The auto-dismiss clock is not reliably held while keyboard focus is inside the surface: `mouseleave` resumes the timer with no check on `document.activeElement`, whereas `focusout` does check hover — so a hover-then-tab-to-Undo-then-pointer-away sequence lets the snackbar auto-dismiss while the user's focus is sitting on the Undo button, destroying both the affordance and the focus position.

strengths: State machine is real, not decorative: absent/entering/visible/leaving/reverted live in `data-state`, drive the CSS, and gate every transition (`leave()` and `onUndo()` both early-return unless state is `visible`). Verified live — interrupting an exit animation with a new save yields exactly 1 node in state `visible` that still auto-dismisses correctly, guarded by a `data-cancelled` sentinel that stops the orphaned `afterAnimation` callback from reaching a terminal state.

prefers-reduced-motion genuinely collapses, and I confirmed it rather than trusting the CSS: under `reducedMotion: reduce` the mounted snackbar computes `transform: none` and `animation-duration: 1e-05s` (vs `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,3.23)` / `0.2s` normally). The `@keyframes` redefinition inside the media block really does win, and `afterAnimation()` carries a `setTimeout` fallback so the machine still advances if `animationend` never fires.

The surface is truly mounted and unmounted — `body.appendChild` on commit, `parentNode.removeChild` on every terminal path — never CSS-hidden. Confirmed `document.querySelector('[data-snackbar]')` is null after auto-dismiss, Escape, Dismiss, and Undo.

The pause/resume clock is correctly accounted, not naively restarted: `remaining -= (Date.now() - resumeAt)` on pause, `startClock(remaining)` on resume, with `focusin`/`focusout` as well as hover, plus a post-entrance re-check (`snack.contains(document.activeElement) || snack.matches(':hover')`) that catches a pointer or focus arriving during the 200ms entrance. Live: `data-clock` flips to `paused` on Tab-to-Undo, and the surface survives 7s hovered then dies 6s after unhover.
defects: Focus is never restored. There is no `.focus()` call anywhere in the file — `document.activeElement` is only ever read. Worse, `inertize()` sets `el.inert = true` while focus is inside, which actively evicts it. Verified live: after keyboard-Undo, after Dismiss, and after Escape, `document.activeElement` is `BODY`. A keyboard user who tabs to Undo and presses Enter is dumped to the top of the document, and the trigger they came from (`#save-btn`) is never re-focused.

The Save button is disabled by `pointer-events: none` (via `.btn--loading`) rather than the `disabled` attribute — confirmed live `saveBtn.disabled === false` during the 900ms flight. It stays in the tab order and stays keyboard-activatable while reading "Saving…" with `aria-busy="true"`, so Enter fires a second `commit()` that a mouse user is blocked from. Mouse and keyboard disagree about whether the control is live.

Hover-pause has no touch counterpart. On touch devices a tap on the snackbar body synthesizes `mouseenter` with no matching `mouseleave`, which parks `data-clock="paused"` and leaves the surface up indefinitely; the only escape is `focusout`/`resume`, which never fires because nothing inside was focused. There is no `pointerdown`/`touchstart` guard and no ceiling on the paused state. (Reasoned from the code path, not touch-emulated.)

Escape is a no-op during the ~200ms `entering` window — the handler guards on `state() === "visible"`. Same for `onDismiss()`, which routes through the same guard, so a fast click on the × mid-entrance is swallowed silently rather than queued.

`note()` is skipped when a new commit interrupts a `leaving` surface: `teardown()` marks it `data-cancelled`, and `finish()` returns before `done()`, so that outcome never reaches the ledger. The surrounding surface silently loses a terminal record it claims to reflect.

`dwellMs()` does `parseFloat(getPropertyValue('--snackbar-dwell'))` with no unit handling — the authored `6000ms` works, but editing the token to the equally idiomatic `6s` silently yields a 6ms dwell. Minor, but it makes the token's contract implicit. Related: `afterAnimation`'s fallback `setTimeout` is never cleared, leaving one dead timer per mounted surface (harmless — the `settled` flag absorbs it).
votes.worst_defect: Focus is never returned to the invoking trigger. No `.focus()` call exists in the file, and `inertize()` (`el.inert = true` + `aria-hidden`) evicts focus from the snackbar before removal — verified live, `document.activeElement` is `BODY` after Undo, Dismiss, and Escape, so a keyboard user is thrown to the top of the document on first use.
